title: Layered Habits & Broken Routines: Soler & Dejar de

sections.content: You know *soler* + infinitive from B1 Unit 5 and B1 Unit 9, *dejar de* + infinitive from B1 Unit 12 and *no dejar de* ('keep on doing') from B2 Unit 25. At C1, everyday speech layers them with aspectual *se* and idiomatic expressions: *Suele tomarse un café cargado antes de leer el periódico de corrido*, *Antes seguía cada receta al pie de la letra, pero dejó de hacerlo cuando empezó a improvisar*. Remember two limits of *soler*: it is defective and is used almost exclusively in the present and imperfect (*suele*, *solía*), never in the preterite (*solió* is not used) or future (*solerá* is avoided). What C1 adds is the emphatic use with verbs of feeling and effect: *no deja de sorprenderme* ('it never ceases to surprise me') stresses that something keeps happening.

sections.title: Combining soler, dejar de and aspectual se
rows: *Suele tomarse un café cargado*; *Solía leerse el diario entero*.
Use *solía* for past habits (never *solió*) and *normalmente* + the tense you need for other times.
*Dejó de seguir la receta al pie de la letra* ('stopped doing').
*No deja de sorprenderme lo bien que improvisa* ('never ceases to').

items.spanish: Carlos suele tomarse un café cargado antes de salir hacia la oficina.
items.english: Carlos usually has a strong coffee before heading to the office.

items.spanish: Antes seguía todas las recetas al pie de la letra, pero dejó de hacerlo al aprender a improvisar.
items.english: Before, she used to follow every recipe to the letter, but she stopped doing it when she learned to improvise.

items.spanish: Solía leerse las noticias de corrido mientras desayunaba.
items.english: He used to read the news straight through while having breakfast.

items.spanish: No deja de sorprenderme cómo siempre encuentra el condimento justo en un apuro.
items.english: It never ceases to surprise me how she always finds the right seasoning in a tight spot.

sections.content: Because *soler* already means 'usually', *normalmente suele tomarse…* sounds heavy, so leave out one of the two. And never conjugate *soler* in the preterite: say *Antes solía cocinar*, not *Antes solió cocinar*.
